the interaction of vegetation and climate change is complex and that vegetation cover change is an important factor in the feedback between climate and land use change.
the urban–wildland interface (UWI), which is the transition zone between wildland and urban area, is a sensitive region to respond to climate change.

the urban–wildland interface area plays a key role in regulating local climate, and the vegetation dynamics in the interface area is more sensitive to human activities and climate warming than the other two areas.

the vegetation–climate interactions in urban–wildland areas are complex, and the effects of climate and land use changes are not necessarily additive, but may even counteract each other.

the vegetation–climate feedback mechanism in the urban–wildland interface is complex, which requires more detailed research on the interaction between land use change and vegetation dynamics in urban areas.
